To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new approach to estimate the pose of a hand from depth data that discriminatively trains a convolutional neural network to output a low-dimensional activation feature given a 2D depth map and uses this activation feature to estimate the hand pose using a novel matrix completion algorithm that exploits spatio-temporal information from a database of activation features and the known pose parameter values.

(a) a low-dimensional feature vector that is discriminative enough for classification can also be used to estimate the pose parameter values, and (b) using a database of such feature vectors and their corresponding pose parameters, we can complete the matrix of pose parameters using the spatio-temporal nearest neighbors of a given activation feature.
we can robustly estimate hand pose parameters from a single depth map using a matrix completion algorithm that uses activation features from a database of synthetic depth maps.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions: 1) a novel method to represent hand poses in a low dimensional space; 2) a novel method for hand pose estimation from depth data using a combination of nearest neighbor search and matrix completion; 3) an efficient implementation of the algorithm that runs at real time on standard computer.

we have developed a method for robust hand pose estimation from depth data that can handle large viewpoint changes, self-occlusions and missing data.
we have developed a robust, real time and efficient approach to estimate hand poses from a depth sensor.
we propose an efficient and robust hand pose estimation algorithm that can be used to track hand pose in real time.

a low dimensional activation vector from a deep network can be used to robustly estimate hand pose.
a discriminative feature representation of depth maps can be used to robustly estimate hand pose parameters.
